summary.text: 昨 means “yesterday” and also refers more broadly to the past. Its received construction combines 日 for the day-related meaning with 乍 as a sound element.

formation.text: This is a phonosemantic compound: 日 contributes the day-related meaning, and 乍 supplies a phonetic cue. Shuowen gives the gloss 壘日也, whose relation to “yesterday” is unclear.

components.text: 日 contributes the day-related semantic category in the received analysis of 昨.

乍 is the phonetic element in the received analysis. Accounts of its own graphic origin differ: one proposes a blade cutting vegetation; Shuowen gives another analysis. The proposed depicted object’s name and pronunciation are not established.

sound_limitation.text: The explicit phonetic analysis supports 乍’s role in 昨. The proposed graphic origin of 乍 does not show that the depicted object’s name sounded like 昨.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings differ in initial and tone; this modern pair alone does not establish the historical sound relation.

In Baxter–Sagart’s Old Chinese reconstructions, the forms share an onset and pharyngealized quality but differ in rhyme and final morphology. The comparison does not independently prove the phonetic role.
The listed Middle Chinese categories differ in rhyme and tone, so they do not supply a direct match between the readings.
sound.component_reading: 崇母、去聲、假攝、麻/禡、開口二等
sound.character_reading: 從母、入聲、宕攝、唐/鐸、開口一等

history.text: The received analysis is 日 plus phonetic 乍. The recorded forms include Small Seal and Warring States manuscript examples, but provide no oracle-bone or bronze forms or sequence of earlier graphic changes for 昨.
The curated image is a modern redraw of 乍 in seal-script style. It illustrates the named sound element; it is neither an ancient artifact nor evidence for 昨’s graphic development.

uncertainties.text: The relation between Shuowen’s gloss 壘日也 and the sense “yesterday” is unexplained.

The phonetic role of 乍 is explicit in the received analysis, but the available sound comparisons do not independently establish that role: the Old Chinese forms differ in rhyme and final morphology, and the Middle Chinese categories differ in rhyme and tone.

senses.period: Dating unresolved; cited in the Shiji passage 昨暮夜
senses.text: In the cited Shiji passage 昨暮夜, 昨 means “yesterday.” The citation establishes this use, but not the first occurrence of the character or word.

senses.period: Eastern Jin and later examples cited
senses.text: 昨 also refers more broadly to the past, as in the Eastern Jin phrase 覺今是而昨非 and a Tang poem. These examples attest the sense but do not show when it developed from “yesterday.”
A brief gloss gives “day,” but the evidence does not establish an independent historical use of 昨 with this meaning.

developments.text: The broader past sense is compatible with an extension from “yesterday,” though the cited examples do not document when or how that development occurred.

limitations.text: The cited uses do not establish the earliest occurrence or precise chronology of either sense. Shuowen’s gloss 壘日也 is retained separately because its relation to these meanings is unexplained.

overview.text: 昨 means “yesterday” and can also refer broadly to the past. In its received construction, 日 contributes the day-related meaning and 乍 supplies a sound cue.

components.text: 乍 is the sound element in the received analysis. Its modern reading differs from 昨’s; an older comparison shares some features but differs in others.

relationships.text: In the received analysis, 日 contributes the day-related semantic category within 昨.
The received analysis explicitly assigns 乍 the phonetic role. Current readings and the supplied Baxter–Sagart comparison provide sound comparisons but do not independently establish that role.
